hook: This monster went undefeated for 13 years. The ending is even more surprising.
story: Aleksandr Karelin, a 130-kilogram Siberian, ruled Greco-Roman wrestling: the ancient style where you may only attack above the waist. His career record: 887 wins, 2 losses. He lifted men his own size overhead and threw them; opponents preferred conceding points to being thrown. Three Olympic golds, under three different flags. Nine world titles, never beaten there. And for six straight years, nobody scored a single point on him.
number: Then came the Sydney 2000 Olympic final, and a man called Rulon Gardner: an American raised milking cows on a dairy farm, with no major titles to his name. Gardner scored one point. And gave up none.
closer: Karelin lost, one to nothing: his first defeat in thirteen years. He walked off the mat and never wrestled again.
